title: Repository Inflation (Child-Entity Repositories)
pattern: Creating database repositories for child entities inside an aggregate, allowing direct database access to elements inside the aggregate boundary.
why_bad: Breaches the encapsulation of the Aggregate. By bypassing the Aggregate Root (`Order`), client code can modify child elements (`OrderLine`) directly without the root validating the overall aggregate invariants (e.g., verifying that the total order amount does not exceed a limit).
detection: Traits or Structs acting as Repositories for entities that are not Aggregate Roots.
counterexample: Highly specialized performance optimizations where loading the entire root to change a single child is an unacceptable bottleneck.
source: *Eric Evans - Domain-Driven Design (2003)*, Chapter 6, "Repositories" (Provide repositories only for aggregates, p. 151); *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 12, "Repositories".
